meaning.evidence: "He averaged six lectures a week, delivered in twenty-nine different countries" preserves the unusual productivity details, alongside the institutions, dates and family history.

sense.evidence: "bringing in prohibition" correctly renders enactment of the legislation.

authenticity.evidence: "the sheer amount of work Dr. Crafts got through" sounds naturally conversational without forced Australian idiom.

register.evidence: "He wrote prolifically on moral questions" typifies an almost entirely standard obituary, far lighter than level 4.

tone.evidence: "Supporters of his policies credited him" keeps the source's careful attribution rather than endorsing the claims outright.

flow.evidence: "One curious title among the many less surprising ones was "Rhetoric Made Racy."" smoothly carries the original's dry aside.

variety.evidence: "spoke out", "tried to stop" and "staying there from then on" vary the prose without a repeated conversational tic.

problems.quote: He wrote prolifically on moral questions.
problems.original: He was a prolific writer on moral questions.
problems.why: The retelling remains formal standard English almost throughout and misses the requested strong Australian vernacular.

A.summary: A complete, polished obituary that preserves the source's character and attributions but barely supplies the level-4 voice.

meaning.evidence: "he'd been chief editor of the Twentieth Century Quarterly since 1896" and "twenty-nine different countries" retain the detailed career record.

sense.evidence: "had a big hand in getting prohibition through" correctly conveys an influential part in enactment.

authenticity.evidence: "The mob on the other side" and "ciggies" fit a credible Australian spoken account.

register.evidence: "reckoned", "stayed put" and "having a go" give a sustained Australian conversational voice, though slightly restrained for level 4.

tone.evidence: "aged 73" and "Those on side with him, though, reckoned" maintain the death notice's seriousness and balance under the slang.

flow.evidence: "His pen and his voice barely got a rest in the last fifty years" carries the source's image easily aloud.

variety.evidence: "rein in", "stayed put" and "a steady stream of papers" offer varied phrasing across the long obituary.

essence.evidence: "there's this odd one that crops up: "Rhetoric Made Racy."" keeps the source's wry detail as well as its biographical arc.

B.summary: An especially smooth, respectful conversational obituary, faithful to the facts and the original's dry character, with a slightly restrained level-4 voice.

meaning.evidence: "He finished at Wesleyan in 1869 and at the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871" keeps the education chronology, with the ministry changes and other career specifics also preserved.

sense.evidence: "a fair whack of the credit" correctly renders a substantial attributed role in passing legislation.

authenticity.evidence: "had a red-hot go" and "sheer hard yakka" use familiar Australian idiom in appropriate contexts.

register.evidence: "his dad's church", "a stack" and "durries" sustain a strong Australian vernacular without exceeding vulgarity 1.

tone.evidence: "died of pneumonia in a hospital here today. He was 73" retains the serious death announcement; the more vivid phrasing elsewhere respects the source's character sketch.

flow.evidence: "who ran the International Reform Bureau as its superintendent for 28 years after founding it himself, and who was known far and wide" makes a rather crowded opening sentence.

variety.evidence: "a fair whack", "a red-hot go", "hard yakka" and "won't raise an eyebrow" are varied rather than one repeated flourish.

essence.evidence: "those were just a few of the things his tireless reforming zeal took aim at" keeps the original's closing portrait of the tireless reformer.

problems.quote: who ran the International Reform Bureau as its superintendent for 28 years after founding it himself, and who was known far and wide
problems.original: for 28 years superintendent of the International Reform Bureau which he founded, and widely known
problems.why: The long chain of relative clauses makes the opening harder to say than the rest of the retelling.

C.summary: A faithful, strongly Australian obituary with well-varied idiom and intact dignity; its opening is less fluent than B's.
